title: Developer Experience: SDK Guides, Quickstarts, API Examples, Docs Site Ops, Top Support Issues & Canonical Fixes
author: Aisha Kapoor
content:
Summary:

This document defines the consolidated standards, templates, and operating procedures for all Developer Experience (DevEx) documentation maintained by the eng-developer-experience team. It covers: SDK guides, quickstarts and templates, canonical API examples, docs-site publishing procedures, and the canonical list of top support issues + fixes that should be surfaced in docs and support playbooks.

Purpose and scope:

- Purpose: Provide a single, maintainable source of truth so SDK authors, technical writers, and engineers produce consistent, production-ready docs that reduce support load and accelerate developer time-to-value.
- Scope: All SDK and quickstart content (Python, JavaScript/Node, Go, Java), API examples, docs-site operational tasks (staging -> prod), and the canonical top-issues list used by support, SDK owners, and the docs team.

Ownership and cadence:

- Primary owner: eng-developer-experience (Documentation & SDKs)
- Secondary owners: eng-platform (site infra), eng-serving-runtime (model-specific examples), customer-success (support escalation items)
- Review cadence: Quarterly review of SDK guides and top-issues table; ad-hoc updates for breaking API changes or security fixes.

Standards for all SDK guides and quickstarts:

1) Title and TOC
   - Short, goal-oriented title (e.g., "Quickstart: Python SDK — Text Generation in 5 Minutes").
   - Include an H1, short one-paragraph intro, and an explicit TOC for pages longer than 600 words.

2) Intro and expected outcome
   - One-paragraph intro that states audience, prerequisites, and the outcome.
   - Prereqs must be explicit (SDK version, API key config, minimum account tier, network egress).

3) Code-first examples
   - Provide minimal working examples for the happy path in each supported language: Python, JavaScript/Node, Go, and Java (if applicable).
   - Each example must include: installation, authentication, minimal request, response sample, and error handling/edge-case note.

4) Security & privacy guidance
   - Call out where to store API keys (e.g., environment variables, secrets manager) and any data residency constraints.

5) Testing & CI guidance
   - Include a short section showing how to run examples in CI (e.g., use CI-only test keys, rate-limit mocks, or recorded HTTP fixtures).

6) Versioning and compatibility
   - Documented SDK version (pinned in examples), and compatibility with API versions. Include a one-line upgrade note for breaking changes.

Template: SDK guide structure (required headings)

- H1: Title
- Short intro (audience + outcome)
- Prerequisites
- Quickstart: minimal example (Python first, then others)
- Full example: advanced usage + config options
- Error handling & troubleshooting
- Security considerations
- Testing & CI snippet
- Changelog & compatibility notes
- Related pages and support links

Quickstarts and language examples (canonical snippets)

- Python (pip):
  - Installation: pip install redwood-inference
  - Minimal example:
    import os
    from redwood import RedwoodClient

    client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ.get("REDWOOD_API_KEY"))
    resp = client.generate(model="rw-base-1", prompt="Write a haiku about latency")
    print(resp.text)

  - Notes: Show streaming snippet and how to set max_tokens, temperature.

- JavaScript (npm):
  - Installation: npm i @redwood/inference
  - Minimal example:
    const { RedwoodClient } = require('@redwood/inference')
    const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY })
    const resp = await client.generate({ model: 'rw-base-1', prompt: 'Summarize the doc in one sentence' })
    console.log(resp.text)

  - Notes: Example for ESM import and streaming via async iterators.

- Go (module):
  - go get github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-go
  - Minimal example pseudo-code showing client creation, request, and response.

API examples & canonical patterns

- Keep examples small (<= 30 lines) and link to longer runnable snippets in the GitHub examples repo.
- Provide a canonical example for: synchronous generation, streaming responses, embeddings, and function/tool-calling patterns.
- For streaming examples, include both client-side consumption and a note about connection timeouts and reconnection backoff.

Docs site operating procedures (staging -> prod)

Purpose: Ensure consistent publishing, review, and rollback mechanisms for the docs site.

1) Branching and PR workflow
   - All content changes must be made on feature branches in the docs repo and submitted as PRs with: description, screenshots (if UI changes), and linked ADRs if relevant.
   - Required approvers: one engineering reviewer (owner of SDK), one technical writer. CI must pass (link-checker, lint, build).

2) Staging preview
   - Every merged PR triggers a staging build. Authors must verify the staging page URL and smoke-test code blocks and links.

3) Accessibility & style checks
   - Run automated lint: docs-linter (checks heading depth, alt text for images, and code-block language tags). Fix warnings prior to merge.

4) Publishing to production
   - Daily scheduled deploy at 02:00 UTC. Critical docs-only hotfixes can be deployed immediately after a green CI and two approvers.
   - If the hotfix addresses a security incident, also notify security@redwood.com and log the change under security-and-compliance/audit-logging.

5) Rollback procedure (if site build breaks)
   - Open an incident in PagerDuty with severity SEV2, revert the last merge commit to main, and roll forward when the fix is validated. Include links to the failed build logs and PR in the incident ticket.

Release checklist for SDK and quickstart updates (pre-publish)

- Update example code to pin the SDK version used in the doc.
- Run examples locally and in a CI doc-preview job.
- Update changelog entry (short paragraph).
- Assign reviewers and confirm accessibility checks are green.

Top support issues and canonical fixes (2025-2026)

- This table lists the highest-volume issues reported to support in the last 12 months and the canonical doc or fix that should be referenced or applied. Keep this table up-to-date; owners listed are responsible for triage and doc updates.

| Issue ID | Symptom | Root cause | Canonical fix / Doc | Owner |
|---------:|---------|------------|---------------------|-------|
| DX-101 | SDK auth failures (401) | Missing/expired API key or wrong env var | Docs: "Auth & API keys"; Fix: ensure REDWOOD_API_KEY env var, show example for .env and CI secrets | Miguel Ortega |
| DX-117 | Streaming disconnects | Default TCP idle timeout on some proxies | Docs: Streaming best-practices + recommended client-side backoff; infra: add keepalive header example | Priya Raman |
| DX-129 | Large payload OOM in client | Sending entire dataset as single prompt | Docs: "Best practices for batching and embeddings" with sample batching code snippets | Evan Clarke |
| DX-143 | Inconsistent embedding similarity | Different normalization/embedding model mismatch | Docs: "Embeddings compatibility"; recommend model and normalization pipeline, include repro snippet | eng-serving-runtime |
| DX-156 | 429 rate limit errors | Unexpected burst traffic from naive retry logic | Docs: "Rate limits & retry policies"; canonical retry-backoff implementation (exponential with jitter) | engineering |

Canonical fixes (examples)

- Auth 401: Provide code showing explicit error handling and a diagnostic CLI snippet: redwood diagnose --check-auth (returns IAM/account info and token expiry).
- Streaming: Add example restoring partial state using continuation tokens and show client reconnection pattern with linear backoff up to 30s.
- Batching for embeddings: Include Python snippet that iterates a large list into chunks of N tokens or M items (configurable).

How to update this doc and the top-issues table

1) If you are the owner of an SDK or example that appears in the table, create a PR against this doc with the new details and an updated created_at/last_updated date.
2) Add a short entry in the changelog section describing the reason for the change and link to the support ticket if applicable.

Appendix: Useful commands and snippets

- Local preview (node-based site):
  git checkout -b doc/update-quickstart
  yarn install && yarn build:preview
  # visit staging url in the preview job

- Example CI snippet (GitHub Actions):
  - name: Docs preview
    uses: actions/checkout@v3
  - name: Build docs
    run: yarn build:preview
  - name: Run link checker
    run: yarn docs-linter --report

- Diagnostic example for support to run when troubleshooting auth issues:
  REDWOOD_API_KEY=abc123 redwood diagnose --check-auth --format=json

Related pages:

- devex: Quickstart repository (internal): https://github.com/redwood-inference/devex-examples
- Docs site operating procedures: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/docs-site/developer-experience-docs-site-operating-procedures-2026.json

Contact and escalation:

- For content ownership/questions: eng-developer-experience@redwood.com
- For immediate SDK regressions or high-severity support issues: PagerDuty (oncall: devex-sdk-owner)
